title: THE LOOP CARD — The UCT Method · Lesson 1
tagline: Regime → Scan → Setup → Size → Manage → Review: the six-station operating loop. Every trade runs all six, in order. Every lesson in this course plugs into exactly one of these boxes.

sections.heading: How this card works
items: Six stations, in order, every trade. The output of each station is the input of the next — the dial grants permission, the scan supplies the name, the catalog names the trade, the stop sets the size, the rules run the exit, the journal grades the loop. A trade that skips a station is not a UCT trade.

Every lesson from here on plugs into exactly one station, and you will be told which one before it starts. Print this card, keep it beside your platform, and re-fill the walk-through at the bottom for every trade until the loop is reflex.

sections.heading: The six stations
items: # | STATION | GOVERNING QUESTION | THE TOOL / NUMBER THAT ANSWERS IT

1 | REGIME | What am I permitted to do today? | The 0-150 UCT Exposure Rating dial, read every morning. The score maps to a GREEN / YELLOW / ORANGE permission band — permission, not prediction. GREEN means more of your playbook is authorized, not that the market goes up.

2 | SCAN | Which names have earned a place on my list? | The nightly scan: Stage-2 pass → ADR% ≥ 4 → dollar-volume floor → RS trend up → ranges tightening. ~3,700 tickers to ~10 names in 20 minutes. A-list = at the pivot within 1-2 days, alert armed at the exact trigger price; B-list = right pattern, needs time.

3 | SETUP | What exactly is this trade, by catalog name? | The firm's setup catalog (4 families) + the five-field card: Context · Pattern · Trigger · Stop · Failure mode. Every entry fires as one of four triggers: BASE BREAKOUT · PREV DAY HIGH BREAK · PREV LOW RECLAIM · RED TO GREEN.

4 | SIZE | How much — derived from the stop, never from conviction? | Account Risk % = Position Size % × Stop Distance % — 2% hard max, under 1% preferred (at 1% risk: 5% stop → 20% position; 10% stop → 10% position). The table: GREEN+A+ 20-25% · YELLOW+A+ 15% · ORANGE+A+ 8% · B-in-ORANGE = skip. Portfolio heat = Σ(entry−stop)×shares ÷ equity, capped at 10% — no new buy above it.

5 | MANAGE | Is the plan intact — and which exit rule fires now? | The stop is an appointment, not a debate. Breakeven at roughly +1R or the first higher low. Partials: first third off at 2-3R into strength; trail the rest — 10-day for fast movers, 10/20-day for EPs, 20/50-day for position holds. Nothing happening for N days is itself an exit. Never add to losers.

6 | REVIEW | What did this trade teach, in a form I can aggregate? | The 7-field journal, filled the day the trade closes: Date · Setup tag · Entry type · Planned R · Exit-vs-plan · Three-axis grade (Idea / Execution / Preparation) · Annotated screenshot. Zero blank fields. P&L is not a grade.

sections.heading: Walk one trade through the loop (fill in before and as you trade)
items: 1 REGIME — Dial score: ______ / 150  →  Band (circle one): GREEN · YELLOW · ORANGE
2 SCAN — From (circle one): A-list · B-list  ·  Alert armed at exact trigger: $________
3 SETUP — Catalog name: ______________  Family: ______________  Trigger (circle one): BASE BREAKOUT · PREV DAY HIGH · PREV LOW RECLAIM · RED TO GREEN
4 SIZE — Stop distance: ______%  ×  Position size: ______%  =  Account risk: ______% (max 2%)  ·  Book heat after entry: ______% (max 10%)
5 MANAGE — Stop (the appointment): $________  ·  Breakeven move at (~+1R): $________  ·  First-third target (2-3R): $________  ·  Trail (circle one): 10-day · 20-day · 50-day
6 REVIEW — Journaled day of close, all 7 fields (Y/N): ____  ·  Grade — Idea: ____  Execution: ____  Preparation: ____

footer_rule: Run the loop in order, every trade, no exceptions — permission before tickers, name before size, stop before shares, journal before the next trade.

GREEN + A+ | 20–25% | full playbook authorized
YELLOW + A+ | 15% | rights reduced — trim count and size
ORANGE + A+ | 8% | best names only, smallest size

Every cell | Account Risk % = Position Size % × Stop Distance % | 2% hard max — prefer under 1%

sections.heading: 4 · PORTFOLIO HEAT vs THE 10% CAP
items: Account equity today: $______
Open risk = Σ (entry − stop) × shares across every open position: $______
Portfolio heat = open risk ÷ equity × 100 = ______ % (hard cap: 10%)
Correlation check — same-theme names counted as ONE risk budget (five AI names is one trade)? YES / NO → adjusted heat: ______ %
Heat headroom for new buys: 10% − adjusted heat = ______ % (no new buy while over the cap)
Drawdown protocol status — equity vs high-water mark: ______ % → (circle) NORMAL / −5%: halve all new sizes / −10%: pilot-or-paper only

sections.heading: 5 · MONDAY GATE — ALL BOXES OR NO ORDERS
items: Dial read and band circled BEFORE any chart or ticker was opened
Sunday deep scan done — A-list charts annotated with exact entry and stop, alerts armed at trigger prices
Every A-list candidate carries a letter grade (no letter, no size)
Every planned position sized stop-first through the formula — never size first, stop back-fitted second
No single planned trade risks more than 2% of the account (under 1% preferred)
Heat computed, correlation-adjusted, and under 10% before any buy-stop goes in

sections.heading: 6 · WHAT CHANGES THIS PLAN MID-WEEK — BAND-FLIP TRIGGERS
items: This page is not a weekly contract — it dies the moment the band flips, and the new band's column applies immediately.

DOWNGRADE: a distribution-day cluster (4–6 inside ~25 sessions) legally ends an uptrend; a mid-week band drop revokes new-buy rights and re-keys every ceiling on this page — open positions get managed to plan, pending orders get cancelled.
UPGRADE: a follow-through day (day 4–7 off the low, up big on higher volume) re-opens buying at PILOT size only — first rung of Pilot → Half → Full → Overweight, each rung paid for by the last.
EQUITY TRIGGERS fire regardless of band: at −5% of equity halve all new sizes; at −10% go pilot-or-paper only — decided now, while calm, because it cannot be decided during.
My one sentence — what specifically flips this plan mid-week, written now while calm: ________________________________________________

footer_rule: GREEN is permission, not prophecy — and when the band flips mid-week, this page gets re-written, not argued with.

title: THE R-MULTIPLE LEDGER
tagline: The UCT Method standing trade log — every trade priced in units of risk. 1R = the dollars you planned to lose if the stop hits. Nothing else.

sections.heading: HOW TO LOG
items: Fix 1R in dollars BEFORE entry: shares x stop distance. Check it with the formula — Account Risk % = Position Size % x Stop Distance %. Hard max 2% of equity per trade; under 1% is the preference.
The sum of every OPEN row's 1R is your portfolio heat. It never exceeds 10% of equity — if a new row would break 10%, the answer is no trade.
Record the exit in R, not dollars: risk $500, make $1,100 = +2.2R; stopped at plan = -1.0R. Rule Y/N asks one question only — did you follow the written plan, win or lose?
This ledger is the Review station of THE LOOP (Regime > Scan > Setup > Size > Manage > Review). Run the expectancy block below after every 20 rows — that number, not P&L, grades your system.

sections.heading: THE LEDGER
items: Date | Ticker | Setup name | 1R ($ planned risk) | Exit date | Result (R) | Rule Y/N

sections.heading: EXPECTANCY SELF-CALC — run after every 20 trades
items: Trades logged (minimum 20): ______
Wins: ______  ·  Win rate = wins / trades: ______ %
Losses: ______  ·  Loss rate = losses / trades: ______ %
Avg win = sum of all winning R / number of wins: ______ R
Avg loss = sum of all losing R / number of losses (write as a positive number): ______ R
EXPECTANCY = (Win rate x Avg win R) - (Loss rate x Avg loss R) = ______ R per trade
Rule-followed rate = Y rows / total rows: ______ %

sections.heading: READ YOUR NUMBER
items: Worked example: 45% x 2.0R - 55% x 1.0R = +0.35R/trade — a system that loses more often than it wins and still prints money. That is the casino math; you own the equation, not the next hand.
Positive expectancy + a Rule column full of Y = keep trading it. Negative expectancy, or a column of N's, = stop sizing up and return to the risk-math module before the next trade.
Never add to losers — averaging down is manually growing the Avg-loss term of your own equation.

footer_rule: A planned 1R loss taken on rule is the system working, not the system breaking — this ledger grades your process, because P&L is not a grade.

title: THE PLACEMENT DIAGNOSTIC — The Five Leaks
tagline: The UCT Method · Module 1, Lesson 4 — ten honest answers locate the leak holding your equity curve at zero.

sections.heading: How to Take It
items: Answer every question Y or N against your last 20 real trades — pull the journal, not the memory. No journal to pull? Answer from what you can prove; the blanks are themselves data.
A Yes is not a verdict on you. It is a location: five leaks, ten questions, two per leak.
Score honestly. A flattered diagnostic sends the wrong leak to your capstone.

sections.heading: Before You Answer — Read the Dial

Its band (GREEN / YELLOW / ORANGE): ______
If you had to look up how to find it, count that as your first data point.

sections.heading: WORKED EXAMPLE — FLAT BASE BREAKOUT
items: Field | Example entry

Worked example — SETUP: Flat Base Breakout (Bases & Breakouts) · CONTEXT: GREEN band, Stage 2, RS line at highs, 5-week flat base under $50 · PATTERN+TRIGGER: tight range 46-49.80, BASE BREAKOUT over $50.00 on volume · STOP: $46.90 under the base low → 6.2% → 16% position at 1% risk · FAILURE MODE: closes back inside the base within 3 days on rising volume — exit, don't argue · 2R check: $56 target ÷ risk ≈ 2.0R — passes.
2 Precondition | Stage-2 pass; each pullback smaller than the last; volume dried up into the base; pivot drawn to the tick at $50.00
3 Trigger | BASE BREAKOUT — buy-stop $50.10, valid only on expanding volume through the pivot
4 Stop | $47.50, under the final contraction low = pattern objectively broken; 5.2% stop distance
5 Target / R | First target $55.30 under next resistance = 2.0R → meets the 2R minimum; at 1% account risk: 1% ÷ 5.2% ≈ 19% position — inside the GREEN + A+ 20-25% cap

title: THE SIZING GATE — Module 5 Checkpoint
tagline: Ten problems. 100% to pass. The course's hard gate on its most dangerous skill — a trader who sizes wrong one time in ten is not 90% safe, he is unsafe.

sections.heading: Member
items: Attempt #: ______

sections.heading: How This Gate Works
items: Fold this page to cover every ANSWER line. Solve each problem cold on scratch paper, then uncover and grade. Copying the printed work is passing someone else's gate.

The formula: Account Risk % = Position Size % × Stop Distance % — so Position Size % = Account Risk % ÷ Stop Distance %. Then Position $ = Position Size % × Account, and Shares = Position $ ÷ Entry (always round DOWN).
Sequence is law: stop first, distance second, size last. The stop marks the price where the thesis is wrong — you never pick a size and back-fit a stop inside the noise.
Hard limits on every problem: account risk ≤ 2% per trade (under 1% preferred) · regime ceiling from the table below · total portfolio heat ≤ 10%.

sections.heading: Regime Size Ceilings (check on every problem)
items: Regime | A+ setup — max position size | B setup
GREEN | 20–25% | reduced (below A+)
YELLOW | 15% | reduced (below A+)
ORANGE | 8% | SKIP — no B setups in ORANGE

sections.heading: The Ten Problems — find Stop Distance %, Position Size %, Position $, Shares, $ at Risk
items: 1) Account $10,000 · GREEN · A+ · target account risk 1% · entry $50.00 · structural stop $47.50.
ANSWER: Stop = 5%. Size = 1% ÷ 5% = 20% → $2,000 → 40 shares → 40 × $2.50 = $100 at risk (1.0%). Under the 25% GREEN ceiling — the formula stands.
2) Account $10,000 · GREEN · A+ · target 1% · entry $20.00 · stop $18.00.
ANSWER: Stop = 10%. Size = 1% ÷ 10% = 10% → $1,000 → 50 shares → $100 at risk (1.0%). Twice the stop of #1, half the size, same dollars at risk.
3) Account $8,000 · YELLOW · A+ · target 0.5% · entry $25.00 · stop $24.00.
ANSWER: Stop = 4%. Size = 0.5% ÷ 4% = 12.5% → $1,000 → 40 shares → $40 at risk (0.5%). Under the 15% YELLOW ceiling.
4) Account $25,000 · GREEN · A+ · target 2% · entry $125.00 · stop $115.00.
ANSWER: Stop = 8%. Size = 2% ÷ 8% = 25% → $6,250 → 50 shares → $500 at risk (2.0%). At the 2% hard max AND the top of the GREEN ceiling — legal, but nothing may be added.
5) Account $50,000 · GREEN · A+ · target 1% · entry $80.00 · stop $76.80.
6) Account $100,000 · ORANGE · A+ · target 0.5% · entry $50.00 · stop $46.00.
ANSWER: Stop = 8%. Size = 0.5% ÷ 8% = 6.25% → $6,250 → 125 shares → $500 at risk (0.5%). Fits under ORANGE's 8% ceiling — barely. In ORANGE, small and A+ or nothing.
7) Account $250,000 · GREEN · A+ · target 1% · entry $200.00 · stop $188.00.
ANSWER: Stop = 6%. Size = 1% ÷ 6% = 16.7% → $41,667 → 208 shares → 208 × $12 = $2,496 at risk (~1.0%). The formula does not care how big the account is.
8) Account $75,000 · GREEN · A+ · target 2% · entry $150.00 · stop $132.00.
9) Account $50,000 · GREEN · A+ · target 1.5% · entry $50.00 · stop $48.50. Check the ceiling table before you finalize.

ANSWER: Stop = 3%. The formula says 1.5% ÷ 3% = 50% position — but the GREEN + A+ ceiling is 25%. CAP IT: 25% → $12,500 → 250 shares → $375 at risk (0.75%). The table always outranks the formula: a tight stop never licenses a monster position, because a stop cannot catch an overnight gap — that gap risk is exactly why the ceiling exists.
10) Account $8,000 · GREEN · A+ chart · target 1% · entry $40.00 · honest structural stop $34.00 (under the base low). What do you do?

ANSWER: Stop = 15%. Formula: 1% ÷ 15% = 6.7% → $533 → 13 shares risking $78 — too small to matter. Sizing it to a meaningful 20% ($1,600 / 40 shares) would risk $240 = 3.0%, over the 2% hard max. Correct answer: SKIP. You never shrink the stop to force the trade — invalidation first, size second, and when the two can't agree the answer is no trade.

items: Every size was derived FROM the stop — I never picked a size first
No answer risks more than 2% of the account
Every share count was rounded DOWN
I checked the regime ceiling on all 10 problems (it decided #9)
#10 is marked SKIP — not a tighter stop

title: THE PLAYBOOK TEMPLATE + DEFENSE RUBRIC
tagline: The UCT Method · Capstone (M16) — author your two setups from your own logged data, then defend one live plan through all six LOOP stations: Regime → Scan → Setup → Size → Manage → Review.

sections.heading: HOW THIS CARD WORKS
items: TOP: write the playbook entry for each of your two contracted setups. Your Module 7-14 drill scores and field-week logs pick them — the data votes, not your mood.
Every blank must be numeric and falsifiable — a number a stranger could trade from. "Buy strength, stop below support" fails review.
BOTTOM: build ONE current-market trade plan and score it against the rubric. Compass pre-grades, the owner reviews async — all six rows must read PASS to graduate.

items: Regime + grade | Max position size
GREEN + A+ | 20-25%

sections.heading: TRADE-PLAN DEFENSE RUBRIC — SIX ROWS, EACH PASS/FAIL, ALL SIX TO GRADUATE
items: # · Station | The grader passes it only if | Verdict
1 · REGIME | Today's actual 0-150 UCT Exposure Rating is written down with its GREEN / YELLOW / ORANGE band — today's reading, not "the market looks good" | PASS ☐  FAIL ☐
2 · SCAN | The candidate came from a real scan — nightly Screener run, A-list, or weekend deep scan — and the source is cited | PASS ☐  FAIL ☐

3 · SETUP | The setup is named from the catalog AND graded A+/A/B/C, citing the rubric line that decided the letter (regime alignment · family score · RS rank · catalyst · clean stop) | PASS ☐  FAIL ☐
4 · SIZE | Size is shown BOTH ways and they agree: Account Risk % = Position Size % × Stop Distance % (≤2%) AND the regime × grade cell above — down to the share count | PASS ☐  FAIL ☐
5 · MANAGE | Both exit paths are pre-committed in writing: wrong = the stop price, an appointment not a debate; right = partial at 2-3R + the named trail line | PASS ☐  FAIL ☐

6 · REVIEW / STRESS | "What makes this plan wrong tomorrow?" is answered with a specific invalidation (gap through the stop, regime downgrade, correlation to open book) — not "if it goes down" | PASS ☐  FAIL ☐

sections.heading: BEFORE YOU SUBMIT
items: All five fields on BOTH entries hold numbers a stranger could trade from — zero vague lines
This plan's add keeps portfolio heat ≤ 10% (correlated names share one risk budget)
No new entry inside the pre-report earnings window — date checked on the Calendar
The dial reading cited is TODAY'S, and the plan dies if the band downgrades
Specialization contract signed: one primary setup · two full earnings seasons · 40 journal-logged reps before any expansion
All six rubric rows read PASS — five of six is a fail; remediate the failed station and resubmit

footer_rule: Graduation certifies a defended plan, not videos watched — if any of the six rows fails, the plan fails, and a plan that cannot name what kills it tomorrow is a hope, not a plan.
